Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Summary of customer pain & goals
- Current service (in-house) sees p95 latencies ~200–260ms for 256–512 token responses during peak; spikes to ~500ms when traffic bursts.
- Peak sustained throughput target: ~50 req/s today, expected to grow to ~75 req/s within 3 months.
- Model: customer wants to run an open 13B LLM (Llama 2 style) with multimodal plans later. Concerned about token-level costs and inference scaling.
- Constraints: Data residency (US only), prefer dedicated capacity or private deployment, and strict SLA for checkout flows.

Redwood readout / suggested topology
- SLO targets (proposal): p95 <= 150ms for 512-token responses under normal load; p95 <= 250ms under 2x burst. Throughput: baseline 75 req/s sustained with headroom for 150 req/s burst via autoscale.
- Deployment topology: primary in us-west (closest to your users), warm standby in us-east for failover and cross-region fallback routing.
- Capacity: Dedicated GPU pool (A100-class or equivalent) with autoscaling policy + burst capacity to on-demand. Option for Private (VPC) if you require customer-managed networking.
- Performance levers: int8 quantization, continuous batching with low-latency cutover, KV/prefix caching for commonly used prompts, and model sharding across multi-GPU for large sequence workloads.

Open technical questions (requested from your side)
- Can you share a 24–48 hour sample of production traffic (timestamps, request sizes, typical prompt/response token counts)?
- Do you expect many long-context (>1k tokens) requests during peak?
- Any regulatory constraints on logs retention or tracing PII?

Action items & next steps
1) Alex/Priya: share a 24–48h traffic sample and a canonical sample request/response (anonymized) — link or S3/gs:// is fine. (Target: 2026-11-18)
2) Redwood (Vivek/Rishi): run a perf estimate and initial cost + capacity plan from the sample, include recommended quantization/throughput config. (Target: 2026-11-20)
3) Schedule a 60-min follow-up perf session with traffic replay and focused perf testing (Propose 2026-11-22).
4) Exchange NDAs / procurement contacts if we move to a trial dedicated cluster.

Attachments I added to this thread:
- acme-internal-architecture.png (diagram stub)
- redwood-inference-slo-proposal.pdf (draft SLO and topology)

If this matches your notes, I’ll kick off the perf bench once we have the sample.

Thanks,

Alex / team — quick technical notes before we kick off the perf run.

On quantization and quality
- int8 (dynamic/static) is often a good trade for 13B models; in our experience it reduces memory and increases throughput with minimal quality regression for many instruction-following tasks. That said, we’ll include fp16 and int8 variants during perf tests and provide a simple ROUGE/QA pass rate comparison on your canonical prompts so you can validate.

On failover and routing
- Expected failover (route + warm standby) is typically ~10–20s for new requests if we have prefix/KV caching warmed; cold failover for very long contexts may be slower. For checkout endpoints we can configure sticky routing and an active-standby policy to meet <30s SLO.

Performance tweaks we’ll evaluate in the perf run
- Batching profiles (target batch size vs latency tradeoff)
- Continuous KV prefix caching for common prompts (very effective for chat sequences)
- Model parallel sharding where single-GPU memory is insufficient for long contexts
- Autoscale policy tuning and pre-warming heuristics to handle predictable bursts (holiday sale patterns)

Required inputs from Acme for accurate estimates
- Realistic traffic replay (thank you for the s3 path)
- A few canonical prompts and acceptance criteria (e.g., max p95 latency for checkout = 150ms)
- Any PII redaction rules that should be applied to logs and traces

I’ll start drafting a perf-plan doc and cost/instance estimate once we get the sample.

-Vivek
